liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (4 reviews): Along with Schoolgirl, it is formless: long solos over the chord changes, inoffensive but uninspired; Solo isn't imaginative, but it shows the band's raw power playing straight-ahead rock [3][6][9][10]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (4 reviews): Considered forgettable by this reviewer; Reviewer calls this version a throwaway [6][9][12][13]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Seems to be the first Morning Dew; the version is quite decent; After Jerry sings the line about it not mattering, the band slips into a soothing jam; reviewer says first live performance [3][9]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Morning Dew [15]

## The recordings

- **gd67-01-14.sbd.vernon.9108.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 3 songs; 30 min; rated 3.77/5 by 44 [1]. Said about its sound: Heavy hiss and occasional muddiness; borderline listenable, but picky listeners may struggle; Quite acceptable recording, though worth adjusting the EQ; Old, dirty, not crisp audio, which the reviewer finds adds atmosphere [3][7][8][10][12]
- **gd1967-01-14.sbd.vernon.9108.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 30 min; rated 2.83/5 by 6 [2]

## Around the show

- A distracting flute and a man rapping onstage are noted; reviewer wonders who he was [7]
- A bright day that drew the Haight's freaks to the Polo Fields, which Phil likens to Avebury in England [10]
- Reviewer, then 16, took a bus from the Peninsula; recalls the eucalyptus smell and little of the music [11]
- The show was part of the Human Be-In, which appeared in the reviewer's high school US history textbook [14]
- The performance was at the Human Be-In [1]
- Charles Lloyd played flute on Schoolgirl at the Human Be-In afternoon concert [2]
- Not the best display of 1967 Dead, but still good [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd67-01-14.sbd.vernon.9108.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard to master reel, then an unknown generation, then CDR; via Raoul Duke; seeded to etree by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1967-01-14.sbd.vernon.9108.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MR >?>CDR [2]. Also: Discs from Raoul Duke were shared in the Music Never Stopped Project's April 2002 shn initiative [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1967-01-14 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1967-01-14-grateful-dead-poster/) [16]
- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [Special Guests of The Grateful Dead at The Human Be-In: January 14, 1967 Polo Grounds, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, ](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2024/04/special-guests-of-grateful-dead-at.html) [17]
- Fan art by Leo Holub Grateful Dead: [1967-01-14 Polo Field, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1967-01-14-polo-field-golden-gate-park-san-francisco-ca-usa/) [18]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1967-01-14 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1967-01-14-grateful-dead-poster-14/) [19]
